name: Magnolias and tulip trees
status: 4 archetypal species (full list archived in docs/plant_archive)
notes: Magnolias are beetle-pollinated — the oldest flowering-plant pollination on Earth — with big cream, white or pink cups; the ledger's beetle count sets their seed. Fruit cones with red seeds taken by birds. Asian, Himalayan, eastern North American and a few tropical species.

canopy.name: Southern magnolia

repro.note: beetle-pollinated: reads the ledger's beetle count, not bees

canopy.source: SE US coastal plain; 20–30 m. Glossy evergreen; huge cream flowers. Kew POWO for the name; standard floras for range.

traits.leaf_shape: simple or compound broad leaves, most deciduous in cold bands
traits.trunk: single trunk dividing into a rounded crown
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.notes: grey to grey-brown, smooth on young trees, becoming scaly with small thin plates on old trunks

leaf.notes: very glossy thick leathery dark green ellipses; underside felted rusty brown; the two-tone signature

flower.form: huge cream-white bowls 20-30 cm across, 6-12 thick petals, crown of yellow stamens

fruit.form: cone-like knobbly aggregate 8-12 cm, greenish turning rusty, splitting to hang bright red seeds on threads

appearance.seasonal: evergreen; old leaves drop in spring; none
appearance.silhouette: broad dense dark pyramid to rounded dome, foliage to the ground, glossy highlights; huge white flowers dotted on the canopy in early summer
appearance.refs: Wikipedia Magnolia grandiflora; Flora of North America; Missouri Botanical Garden

canopy.name: Yulan magnolia

repro.note: beetle-pollinated: reads the ledger's beetle count, not bees

canopy.source: central China; 10–15 m. White goblets before the leaves. Kew POWO for the name; standard floras for range.

traits.leaf_shape: simple or compound broad leaves, most deciduous in cold bands
traits.trunk: single trunk dividing into a rounded crown
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.notes: smooth pale grey bark, slightly roughened with age; grey-brown twigs with big furry silver buds

leaf.notes: broad obovate leaves with an abrupt short point, mid green, paler beneath; appear after the flowers

flower.form: upright pure white goblet/tulip flowers 12-15 cm, 9 tepals, on bare branches before leaves

fruit.form: knobbly cylindrical aggregate 8-12 cm, pinkish-brown, red seeds

appearance.seasonal: deciduous; yellow-brown in autumn; bare grey branches covered in white goblets in early spring
appearance.silhouette: small to medium rounded tree, often multi-stemmed, a cloud of white cups on bare grey branches in early spring, then a leafy dome
appearance.refs: Wikipedia Magnolia denudata; Flora of China; Kew POWO

canopy.name: Campbell's magnolia

repro.note: beetle-pollinated: reads the ledger's beetle count, not bees

canopy.source: E Himalayan cloud forest; 20–30 m. Pink cups the size of dinner plates on bare branches. Kew POWO for the name; standard floras for range.

traits.leaf_shape: simple or compound broad leaves, most deciduous in cold bands
traits.trunk: single trunk dividing into a rounded crown
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.notes: grey to grey-brown, smooth, slightly fissured on old trunks

leaf.notes: large elliptic-obovate leaves, mid green above, paler and slightly hairy beneath; after flowers

appearance.seasonal: deciduous; yellow in autumn; pink dinner-plate flowers on bare branches late winter to early spring

canopy.name: Tulip tree

repro.note: beetle-pollinated: reads the ledger's beetle count, not bees

canopy.source: E North American cove forest; 35–50 m. Magnolia family; tallest eastern hardwood; tulip flowers. Kew POWO for the name; standard floras for range.

traits.leaf_shape: simple or compound broad leaves, most deciduous in cold bands
traits.trunk: single trunk dividing into a rounded crown
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.notes: pale grey-brown with regular, interlacing, flat-topped ridges and deep furrows; young trees smooth grey with white streaks

leaf.notes: square-cut four-lobed leaves with a notched flat tip (tulip outline), bright green, on long petioles that flutter

flower.form: upright tulip-shaped cups 5 cm, pale yellow-green with an orange band at the base of each petal

fruit.form: upright cone-like clusters of winged tan samaras, persist through winter

appearance.seasonal: deciduous; clear bright golden yellow in autumn
appearance.silhouette: the tallest eastern hardwood: a huge straight columnar trunk clear of branches for 25 m, narrow oblong crown; a bare mast in winter with upright cone clusters
appearance.refs: Wikipedia Liriodendron tulipifera; Flora of North America; USFS Silvics
